items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: I was away with Walter Pichon... when we were working with Pichon

ctx.x: You see them fellas when they couldn't play a piece, or remember a piece, they had a good air and they make a run or something, you know, fill it in. But trumpet players like Lionel, or I'd say my friend Leo, or Manuel Perez, or Norma Twy, or Maurice Duran, or Willie Paggio. Well that's a class of Lionel.

I'll tell you another good trumpet player, he played Dixieland too. He used to play with, I can't think of that man's name right now, he used to play with Pichon, when we were working with Pichon. From here? Yeah, he lived uptown. He and Louis, to me, he's a very good friend. He's got with Gaudet. Gaudet, that's right.
We had a boy here playing just like Gaudet, just coming, well anyhow him, he'd been sick in the hospital and he's out now, Joe Bentley.

items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: Elec called me and asked me about the job... myself to go around there.

ctx.x: Well from what I can remember, I hope I have it right, the early big guard came and asked me if I wanted to work with him. So, well I had been playing with big bands before then.

Well let me tell you the story. You know more about it than me. Elec went to Peterson's music store to see about some drumsticks or something. And Peterson said, Elec, you all playing anywhere? No. They want a band down at the Melody Inn for Mr. Highdown. So, Elec said, you know, you can go and see about the job. So, Elec called me and asked me about the job. And he said, you know, you can go and see about it. So, I told him, go and see about it. So, he got lying there, I got joys getting off, and myself to go…
So, in other words, it was a big odd job.
